x: The individual title, appropriately on his home course, was won by Ronny Wallwork with Shaun Lightman 2nd and a surprised Arthur Jones 3rd. Ray Middleton was first Belgrave man home hotly pursued by Bob Barnes.

Besides Ray others in the fight for a place will probably be Ronnie Wallwork (The Commonwealth title holder), Shaun Lightman (Metropolitan W.C.), Roy Lodge (Bromsgrove & Redditch A.C.), Bryan Eley (Bristol W.C.) and Jake Warhurst (Sheffield U.H.).
An early pace setter, Eric Taylor, led for 10 miles before being caught by Carl Lawton, who was last man out of Leicester, and Shaun Lightman.

Shaun Lightman and Carl Lawton battled once again but this time it was Shaun who got the verdict. With Ray Middleton and Allan Callow backing up, Bels took the team and there was also some good walking by the Johns Dunsford and Hall, who came in together with Dave McMullen not far behind.
In the 20 kilo's they were led home by John Hall, well behind Shaun Lightman, and John Dunsford despite his 50 kilo's a week earlier managed a commendable performance.
Carl Lawton finished 3rd to Shaun Lightman, having allowed Selby to pass him with three miles to go. John Moullin was a not far behind 5th and Dave King was 19th.

Shaun Lightman was the first leader, a position which he held for much of the race. Carl Lawton made an emergency stop in Croydon to pick up 2p on the road, taking great care that Johnny Morris, this time in the attendants seat on a bicycle, was not there first.

Shaun Lightman was the winner in this event and broke the record in the process. Carl Lawton was our highest placing, although there was some good performances from promising youngsters, John Hall, Bromley and Bennett.

Shaun Lightman managed to break away from Roy (I've forgotten what my heels are for) Court to win and Lawton held off Mal Tolley for third. Ray Middleton powered back onto the scene in 7th place and Len and John brought in our team for another team victory.

Shaun Lightman took the lead after 3 miles and was never headed whilst Carl retook Amos Seddon for 3rd. Leicester packed their first three in nine but we powered in by one point with our usual scoring four despite the return of Allan Callow, and Ray Middleton leaving the road at one time to water the flowers.
With an open team match in conjunction, we turned out six walkers for this race . Shaun Lightman led from start from finish with Carl Lawton similarly holding 2nd place.
This event which had earlier been postponed due to a closed dressing room was eventually held with Shaun Lightman getting the verdict. We only had three starters and so had no team chance.
John Hall finished 4th to Shaun Lightman.
John Hall clocked 23:32.2 for 3rd place in a 5km at Crystal Palace on December 11th. Winner was Shaun Lightman (Met) 22:02.0

Shaun Lightman (Met WC) had an incredible weekend over the spring holiday. He won the Leicester Mercury 20 Miles on the Saturday, and then collected the Inter-Counties double at Crystal Palace on Sunday May 25th/ Monday May 26th with 45:08 for 10km and 12:45 for 3km.
Carl held off fast finishing Shaun Lightman (Met. WC) to finish in a very good time although not as fast as his winning time in the G.L.C. race.
At half way Carl and his old rival Shaun Lightman were in the lead, and on a long steady climb Carl pulled away and increased his lead to win comfortably - his third in a row.
At the halfway point there was no Olly, he had been disqualified and Carl with Shaun Lightman (Met WC) and Roger Mills (Ilford AC) were at the head of affairs.
While the Heathens shocked us by turning out Shaun Lightman, our own Carl Lawton had still not arrived as the contestants were being marshalled for the start.
